newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi cement output to rise to 22 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Saudi cement output to rise to 22 mln tonnes.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's cement production is expected to reach 22 million tonnes a year by the end of the century, well above projected local demand of up to 17.50 million tonnes, the industry and electricity minister said.
Hashem bin Abdullah bin Hashem Yamani said Saudi's cement output was 16 million tonnes in 1996 -- the same as average domestic consumption in 1995 and 1996.
"Average demand for cement up to the year 2000 is expected to be between 15.75 and 17.50 million tonnes a year while total production is expected to be 22 million tonnes," he said.

Yamani was speaking at the long-delayed inauguration on Wednesday of Saudi Cement Co's expansion project in Hofuf, one of several schemes underway in the kingdom which has eight large publicly-traded cement companies.
"These companies have been able to cover the needs of the local market for cement and also export to outside markets. Exports in 1996 reached 2.3 million tonnes," Yamani said.
His comments were carried by the state Saudi Press Agency.

Cement production in Saudi Arabia, the region's largest economy and the world's biggest oil exporter, started in 1958. Several firms, trying to keep up with rising domestic demand, are involved in expansion projects worth more than $1 billion.
Saudi Cement Co's board member Khaled bin Suleiman al-Olayan said the firm's $266 million expansion raises capacity to 4.35 million tonnes a year, up 1.1 million tonnes.
Company officials had said the expansion made it the biggest cement producer in the kingdom.

The project -- carried out by German group Kloeckner Humboldt Deutz AG (KHD) -- was originally due to be completed in September 1995 but was delayed after KHD discovered that executives at its Wedag subsidiary had covered up losses linked to construction of the plant.
KHD said in December last year that it has delivered the cement plant and that Saudi Cement Co has waived all late fees for the delayed project.
